   394	We define a special class of measurements that are relevant to the soundness
   395	properties of the low-degree test.
   396	
   397	\begin{definition}[Low-degree polynomial measurements]
   398	  \label{def:ld-meas}
   399	  Define $\polymeas{m}{d}{q}$ to be the set of POVM measurements whose outcomes
   400	  correspond to (individual) degree-$d$ polynomials of $m$ variables over
   401	  $\F_q$.
   402	  More generally, for an integer $\ldc$ and tuples $m=(m_1, m_2, \ldots,
   403	  m_\ldc)$, $d=(d_1, d_2, \ldots, d_\ldc)$ and $q=(q_1, q_2, \ldots, q_\ldc)$,
   404	  we let $\simulpolymeas{m}{d}{q}{\ldc}$ be the set of measurements $G =
   405	  \{G_{g_1,\, g_2,\, \ldots\,,\, g_\ldc}\}$ such that for $i\in\{1, 2, \ldots,
   406	  \ldc\}$, $g_i$ is a polynomial $g_i:\F_{q_i}^{m_i} \rightarrow
   407	  \F_{q_i}$ with individual degree $d_i$ (see \Cref{sec:ld-encoding} for a definition of individual degree). 
   408	\end{definition}
   409	
   410	Quantum soundness of a version of the classical low-degree test for polynomials of low \emph{total} degree was claimed
   411	in~\cite{natarajan2018low}, building on an analysis of a three-prover version of the test in~\cite{vidick2016three}. Unfortunately there is a gap in the soundness analysis of this test. For our construction we use the low individual degree test, whose quantum soundness is shown in~\cite{ML20} and generalized in~\cite{ji2021quantum}. We state the result in the form that is most directly useful for us, and show how the stated result follows from~\cite{ji2021quantum}.
   412	
   413	\begin{theorem}[Quantum soundness of the simultaneous classical low-degree test]
   414	  \label{lem:ld-soundness}
   415	  There exists a function $\delta_{\ld}(\eps, q, m, d, \ldc) = a (dm \ldc)^a (\eps^b + q^{-b} + 2^{-bmd})$ for universal constants $a\geq 1$ and $0<b\leq 1$ 
   416	such that the following
   417	  holds.
   418	  For all $\eps > 0$ and parameter tuple $\ldparams = (q, m, d, \ldc)$, for all
   419	  projective strategies $(\psi,A,B)$ that succeed with probability at least
   420	  $1-\eps$ in the game $\game^\ld_\ldparams$, there exists measurements
   421	  \[G^w \in \simulpolymeas{m}{d}{q}{\ldc}\] on $\mH_w$, for
   422	  $w\in\{\alice,\bob\}$, such that
   423	  \begin{equation*}
   424	    \begin{split}
   425	      A^{\Point,\, u}_{a_1,\, a_2,\, \ldots\,,\, a_\ldc}
   426	      & \abc[\delta_{\ld}]
   427	      G^\bob_{[(g_1(u),g_2(u),\ldots,g_\ldc(u)) = (a_1,\, a_2,\, \ldots \,,\, a_\ldc)]}\;,\\
   428	      G^\alice_{[(g_1(u),g_2(u),\ldots,g_\ldc(u)) = (a_1,\, a_2,\, \ldots \,,\, a_\ldc)]}
   429	      & \abc[\delta_{\ld}]
   430				 B^{\Point,\, u}_{a_1,\, a_2,\, \ldots\,,\, a_\ldc}\;,\\
   431	      G^\alice_{g_1,\, g_2,\, \ldots \,,\, g_\ldc}
   432	      & \abc[\delta_{\ld}]
   433	      G^\bob_{g_1,\, g_2,\, \ldots \,,\, g_\ldc}\;,
   434	    \end{split}
   435	  \end{equation*}
   436	  where $\delta_{\ld} = \delta_{\ld}(\eps, q, m, d, \ldc)$, 
   437	  and all three statements are with respect to the state $\ket{\psi}$.
   438	In addition, the first two approximations hold under the uniform distribution over $u\in \F_q^m$,
   439		whereas there is no question distribution associated with the third approximation.
   440	\end{theorem}
   441	
   442	\begin{proof}
   443	Let $\ldparams = (q, m, d, \ldc)$
   444	where $m, d, \ldc \in \N$ are integers, $q \in \N$ is an admissible field size,
   445	and $m$ divides $q$. Let $\Sigma=\F_q$. Let $\code \subseteq \Sigma^q$ be the Reed-Solomon code with degree $d$. Explicitly, $\code$ is the set of all $(p(x_1),\ldots,p(x_n))$ where $p:\F_q\to\F_q$ is a univariate polynomial of degree at most $d$ and $x_1,\ldots,x_n$ are an enumeration of $\F_q$. Then in the (standard) notation from~\cite{ji2021quantum} $\code$ is a linear $[q,d+1,n-d+1]_\Sigma$ code.
   446	
   447	Observe that the two-prover tensor code test, for the code $\code^{\otimes m}$, as described in~\cite[Figure 1 and Figure 2]{ji2021quantum}, is identical to the game $\game^\ld$ with parameters $\ldparams$ and $\ldc=1$, whose decider is presented in Figure~\ref{fig:ld-decider}. This is because 
   448	\begin{enumerate}
   449	\item The \emph{axis-parallel line-versus-point test} from Figure~\ref{fig:ld-decider} is identical to the \emph{axis-parallel lines test} from~\cite[Figure 1]{ji2021quantum}, with the only difference that in Figure~\ref{fig:ld-decider} the roles of A and B are chosen uniformly at random. This is consistent with the two-prover variant of the tensor code test from~\cite[Section 4.1]{ji2021quantum}.
   450	\item The \emph{diagonal line-versus-point test} from Figure~\ref{fig:ld-decider} is identical to the \emph{subcube commutation test} from~\cite[Figure 1]{ji2021quantum}, with again the added symmetrization between players. 
   451	\item The \emph{consistency test} from Figure~\ref{fig:ld-decider} is identical to the \emph{synchronicity test} from~\cite[Figure 2]{ji2021quantum}.
   452	\end{enumerate}
   453	
   454	As a result,~\cite[Theorem 4.7]{ji2021quantum}, in which we choose the parameter $k$ as $k=m^3d$,  immediately yields \Cref{lem:ld-soundness}.
   455	
   456	To conclude it remains to extend the result to the case of general $\ldc$. This is done 
   457	via a standard reduction, following exactly the same steps as the derivation of Theorem 4.43 from Theorem 4.40 in~\cite{NW19}.
   458	\end{proof}

   149	\begin{remark}[Obligations of the linearity-theorem import]
   150		\label{rem:linearity-import}
   151		Theorem~\ref{thm:linearity} is stated in the form proved in
   152		\cite{Natarajan2017Linearity}. Three features are load-bearing for the
   153		proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-4-10}: the error is preserved without
   154		polynomial loss ($\delta$ in the hypothesis becomes $\delta$ in the
   155		conclusion); the linearity of the $\{\mathcal{L}^u\}$ is exact and
   156		holds for all pairs $(u,u')$, not merely on average; and the
   157		hypothesis carries no upper bound on $\delta$, so the theorem may be
   158		applied separately for each pair $(x,z)$ with hypothesis error the
   159		conditional linearity defect given $(x,z)$, a quantity for which no a
   160		priori bound is available. The closeness of $\mathcal{L}^u$ to
   161		$\mathcal{O}^u$ is guaranteed on average over a uniformly random $u$
   162		only; this averaged form suffices because the $\mathcal{L}^u$ enter
   163		the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-4-10} only through averages over $u$.
   164		The quotation of the theorem in \cite{Ji2020MIPStar} differs from the
   165		cited statement in three respects: it inserts the restriction
   166		$0 \le \delta \le 1$, which would block the fiberwise application
   167		just described; it places the closeness conclusion, together with the
   168		exact linearity, under the quantifier ``for all $u, u' \in \F_2^t$'',
   169		a strengthening of the theorem proved in
   170		\cite{Natarajan2017Linearity}; and it appends the identity
   171		$\mathcal{L}^u = \Id$ for $u = 0$. None of the three is reproduced
   172		here: the restriction is dropped, the pointwise closeness is not
   173		used, and the appended identity is instead derived from the
   174		conclusion, since exact linearity at $u = u' = 0$ gives
   175		$(\mathcal{L}^0)^2 = \mathcal{L}^0$, and an idempotent unitary equals
   176		the identity. The import carries two conversion obligations,
   177		discharged in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-4-10}: the theorem is
   178		instantiated with $\rho$ the reduced density operator of
   179		$\ket{\hat\psi}$ on the registers carrying the observables, so that
   180		traces against $\rho$ are expectation values in $\ket{\hat\psi}$; and
   181		the correlation hypothesis and the squared-distance conclusion are
   182		converted to and from the relation $\approx_\delta$ of
   183		Definition~\ref{def:povm-distance} by expanding the square, using
   184		unitarity of the observables, and relabelling the averaged index
   185		pair, at the cost of the constant factors absorbed by that
   186		definition. One obligation remains open and is flagged where it
   187		arises: the ancilla register $\hilb'$ and its state
   188		$\ket{\mathrm{anc}}$ produced by the theorem, which may depend on the
   189		pair $(x,z)$, must be absorbed --- uniformly in $(x,z)$ --- into
   190		zero-state padding of the strategy state, padding that the source
   191		assumes present without construction.
   192	\end{remark}

     4	/-!
     5	# The directly indexed low-degree game
     6	
     7	This module defines polynomial evaluation, questions, answers, and the game
     8	for the directly indexed low-degree interface.
     9	
    10	## References
    11	
    12	The underlying game is `def:ld-game` in
    13	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-105`, with source origin
    14	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    15	-/
    16	
    17	open scoped BigOperators
    18	
    19	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    20	
    21	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    22	open MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries
    23	open MIPStarRE.Quantum
    24	
    25	noncomputable section
    26	
    27	/-- Coefficient lists for a univariate polynomial of degree at most `c` in the
    28	direct scalar field. -/
    29	abbrev DirectDegPoly (D : DirectLdParams) (c : ℕ) :=
    30	  Fin (c + 1) → DirectScalarQ D
    31	
    32	/-- A direct line polynomial evaluates to `a` at `u` when `u` lies on the line
    33	and every parameter presenting `u` gives value `a`.  The universal clause
    34	keeps the zero-direction case explicit. -/
    35	def DirectEvaluatesTo {D : DirectLdParams} {c : ℕ} (line : DirectLineDesc D)
    36	    (f : DirectDegPoly D c) (u : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D)
    37	    (a : DirectScalarQ D) : Prop :=
    38	  (∃ t : DirectScalarQ D, u = line.base + t • line.direction) ∧
    39	    ∀ t : DirectScalarQ D, u = line.base + t • line.direction →
    40	      evalCoefficient f t = a
    41	
    42	/-- Option-completed evaluation of a direct line polynomial.  `none` is an
    43	explicit outcome when the point does not determine an evaluation; no field
    44	value is used as a fallback. -/
    45	noncomputable def directEvalOpt {D : DirectLdParams} {c : ℕ}
    46	    (line : DirectLineDesc D) (u : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D)
    47	    (f : DirectDegPoly D c) : Option (DirectScalarQ D) := by
    48	  classical
    49	  exact if h : ∃ a : DirectScalarQ D, DirectEvaluatesTo line f u a then
    50	    some (Classical.choose h)
    51	  else none
    52	
    53	/-- The typed question alphabet of the directly indexed game. -/
    54	abbrev DirectLdQuestion (D : DirectLdParams) := LdType × DirectLdSpace D
    55	
    56	/-- Canonicalize a common direct sample for one question type.  Irrelevant
    57	coordinates are fixed, so point questions reveal no sampled line index and
    58	axis-line questions reveal no diagonal direction. -/
    59	noncomputable def directLdMap (D : DirectLdParams) :
    60	    LdType → DirectLdSpace D → DirectLdSpace D
    61	  | .point, sample => ⟨sample.point, D.firstIndex, 0⟩
    62	  | .aline, sample =>
    63	      let direction := coordinateDirection sample.index
    64	      ⟨lineRepMap direction sample.point, sample.index, 0⟩
    65	  | .dline, sample =>
    66	      let direction := directPrefixProjection sample.index sample.direction
    67	      ⟨lineRepMap direction sample.point, sample.index, direction⟩
    68	
    69	/-- The directly indexed question distribution.  It has the same uniform
    70	ordered type-pair branches as `ldQuestionDistribution`, but its common sample
    71	contains an actual coordinate index rather than a field seed. -/
    72	noncomputable def directLdQuestionDistribution (D : DirectLdParams) :
    73	    Distribution (DirectLdQuestion D × DirectLdQuestion D) :=
    74	  (uniformDistribution ((LdType × LdType) × DirectLdSpace D)).map fun sample =>
    75	    ((sample.1.1, directLdMap D sample.1.1 sample.2),
    76	      (sample.1.2, directLdMap D sample.1.2 sample.2))
    77	
    78	/-- The directly indexed question law is probabilistic. -/
    79	theorem directLdQuestionDistribution_isProbability (D : DirectLdParams) :
    80	    (directLdQuestionDistribution D).IsProbability := by
    81	  exact (uniformDistribution_isProbability
    82	    ((LdType × LdType) × DirectLdSpace D)).map _
    83	
    84	/-- The answer alphabet of the directly indexed game. -/
    85	inductive DirectLdAnswer (D : DirectLdParams) where
    86	  | pointVals (a : Fin D.k → DirectScalarQ D)
    87	  | alinePolys (a : Fin D.k → Fin (D.d + 1) → DirectScalarQ D)
    88	  | dlinePolys (a : Fin D.k → Fin (D.m * D.d + 1) → DirectScalarQ D)
    89	  deriving DecidableEq
    90	
    91	/-- A finite code for the directly indexed answer alphabet. -/
    92	abbrev DirectLdAnswerCode (D : DirectLdParams) :=
    93	  (Fin D.k → DirectScalarQ D) ⊕
    94	    ((Fin D.k → Fin (D.d + 1) → DirectScalarQ D) ⊕
    95	      (Fin D.k → Fin (D.m * D.d + 1) → DirectScalarQ D))
    96	
    97	/-- Constructor-preserving equivalence between the inductive answer type and
    98	its finite code. -/
    99	noncomputable def directLdAnswerEquiv (D : DirectLdParams) :
   100	    DirectLdAnswer D ≃ DirectLdAnswerCode D where
   101	  toFun
   102	    | .pointVals a => .inl a
   103	    | .alinePolys a => .inr (.inl a)
   104	    | .dlinePolys a => .inr (.inr a)
   105	  invFun
   106	    | .inl a => .pointVals a
   107	    | .inr (.inl a) => .alinePolys a
   108	    | .inr (.inr a) => .dlinePolys a
   109	  left_inv := by intro answer; cases answer <;> rfl
   110	  right_inv := by
   111	    intro answer
   112	    rcases answer with a | a
   113	    · rfl
   114	    · rcases a with a | a <;> rfl
   115	
   116	instance (D : DirectLdParams) : Inhabited (DirectLdAnswer D) :=
   117	  ⟨.pointVals 0⟩
   118	
   119	noncomputable instance (D : DirectLdParams) : Fintype (DirectLdAnswer D) :=
   120	  Fintype.ofEquiv (DirectLdAnswerCode D) (directLdAnswerEquiv D).symm
   121	
   122	/-- Check that a direct-game answer has the constructor required by its
   123	question type. -/
   124	def validDirectLdAnswer {D : DirectLdParams} (t : LdType)
   125	    (answer : DirectLdAnswer D) : Bool :=
   126	  match t, answer with
   127	  | .point, .pointVals _ => true
   128	  | .aline, .alinePolys _ => true
   129	  | .dline, .dlinePolys _ => true
   130	  | _, _ => false
   131	
   132	/-- The directly indexed axis-line versus point acceptance relation. -/
   133	def directAlinePointCondition (D : DirectLdParams)
   134	    (line point : DirectLdSpace D)
   135	    (f : Fin D.k → Fin (D.d + 1) → DirectScalarQ D)
   136	    (a : Fin D.k → DirectScalarQ D) : Prop :=
   137	  ∀ t : DirectScalarQ D,
   138	    point.point = line.point + t • coordinateDirection line.index →
   139	      ∀ j : Fin D.k, evalCoefficient (f j) t = a j
   140	
   141	/-- The directly indexed diagonal-line versus point acceptance relation. -/
   142	def directDlinePointCondition (D : DirectLdParams)
   143	    (line point : DirectLdSpace D)
   144	    (f : Fin D.k → Fin (D.m * D.d + 1) → DirectScalarQ D)
   145	    (a : Fin D.k → DirectScalarQ D) : Prop :=
   146	  ∀ t : DirectScalarQ D,
   147	    point.point = line.point + t • line.direction →
   148	      ∀ j : Fin D.k, evalCoefficient (f j) t = a j
   149	
   150	/-- The directly indexed low-degree win predicate.  It differs from
   151	`ldWinPredicate` only by reading the coordinate index directly from each line
   152	question. -/
   153	noncomputable def directLdWinPredicate (D : DirectLdParams) :
   154	    DirectLdQuestion D → DirectLdQuestion D →
   155	      DirectLdAnswer D → DirectLdAnswer D → Bool :=
   156	  open Classical in
   157	  fun (tA, xA) (tB, xB) a b =>
   158	    if validDirectLdAnswer tA a && validDirectLdAnswer tB b then
   159	      match tA, tB, a, b with
   160	      | .point, .point, .pointVals u, .pointVals v => decide (u = v)
   161	      | .aline, .point, .alinePolys f, .pointVals u =>
   162	          decide (directAlinePointCondition D xA xB f u)
   163	      | .point, .aline, .pointVals u, .alinePolys f =>
   164	          decide (directAlinePointCondition D xB xA f u)
   165	      | .dline, .point, .dlinePolys f, .pointVals u =>
   166	          decide (directDlinePointCondition D xA xB f u)
   167	      | .point, .dline, .pointVals u, .dlinePolys f =>
   168	          decide (directDlinePointCondition D xB xA f u)
   169	      | .aline, .aline, .alinePolys f, .alinePolys g => decide (f = g)
   170	      | .dline, .dline, .dlinePolys f, .dlinePolys g => decide (f = g)
   171	      | _, _, _, _ => true
   172	    else false
   173	
   174	/-- The directly indexed low-degree game at an arbitrary positive dimension.
   175	It is an internal analysis game, not the conditionally linear verifier game
   176	`ldGame`. -/
   177	noncomputable def directLdGame (D : DirectLdParams) : Game where
   178	  QuestionA := DirectLdQuestion D
   179	  QuestionB := DirectLdQuestion D
   180	  AnswerA := DirectLdAnswer D
   181	  AnswerB := DirectLdAnswer D
   182	  μ := directLdQuestionDistribution D
   183	  μ_prob := directLdQuestionDistribution_isProbability D
   184	  decide := directLdWinPredicate D
   185	
   186	/-- The canonical point question associated with a geometric point. -/
   187	def directLdPointQuestionOf (D : DirectLdParams)
   188	    (u : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) : DirectLdQuestion D :=
   189	  (.point, ⟨u, D.firstIndex, 0⟩)
   190	
   191	/-- Total point-answer relabeling used in the direct soundness conclusion.
   192	Wrong-form answers are folded into the zero tuple, exactly as for
   193	`ldPointValuesOrZero`. -/
   194	def directLdPointValuesOrZero (D : DirectLdParams) :
   195	    DirectLdAnswer D → Fin D.k → DirectScalarQ D
   196	  | .pointVals values => values
   197	  | .alinePolys _ => 0
   198	  | .dlinePolys _ => 0
   199	
   200	/-- A simultaneous tuple of bounded polynomials for the directly indexed
   201	game. -/
   202	noncomputable abbrev DirectPolyTuple (D : DirectLdParams) :=
   203	  Fin D.k → PolyIndex D.m (DirectScalarQ D) D.d
   204	
   205	/-- A polynomial-tuple POVM for the directly indexed game. -/
   206	noncomputable abbrev DirectPolyMeasTuple (D : DirectLdParams) (ι : Type*)
   207	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] :=
   208	  Measurement (DirectPolyTuple D) ι
   209	
   210	/-- Evaluate every component of a direct polynomial tuple at a point. -/
   211	def evalDirectPolyTupleAt {D : DirectLdParams}
   212	    (u : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) (g : DirectPolyTuple D) :
   213	    Fin D.k → DirectScalarQ D :=
   214	  fun j => MvPolynomial.eval u (g j).1
   215	
   216	end
   217	
   218	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

     3	/-!
     4	# Soundness for the directly indexed low-degree game
     5	
     6	This module isolates the quantum soundness obligation for the directly indexed
     7	low-degree game.
     8	
     9	## References
    10	
    11	The obligation supports the Chapter 15 combining argument at
    12	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1267-1288`.
    13	-/
    14	
    15	open scoped BigOperators
    16	
    17	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    18	
    19	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    20	open MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries
    21	open MIPStarRE.Quantum
    22	
    23	noncomputable section
    24	
    25	/-- Quantum soundness obligation for the directly indexed low-degree game.
    26	This is the repaired import form proposed in
    27	`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex`, needed by the Chapter 15
    28	combining argument at paper
    29	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1267-1288`.
    30	
    31	This is a formalization auxiliary assertion, not the source-labelled
    32	`lem:ld-soundness`.  Its proof must establish the game-correspondence and
    33	auxiliary-parameter bounds catalogued in the cited gap note; neither is hidden
    34	as a hypothesis here. -/
    35	theorem exists_direct_ld_soundness :
    36	    ∃ a b : ℝ, 1 ≤ a ∧ 0 < b ∧ b ≤ 1 ∧
    37	      ∀ (D : DirectLdParams) (ε : ℝ), 0 < ε →
    38	        ∀ S : Strategy (directLdGame D), S.IsProjective → 1 - ε ≤ S.value →
    39	          ∃ GA : DirectPolyMeasTuple D S.ιA,
    40	            ∃ GB : DirectPolyMeasTuple D S.ιB,
    41	              consistencyDefect
    42	                  (uniformDistribution (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D))
    43	                  (fun u outcome =>
    44	                    heteroKron
    45	                      (((S.A (directLdPointQuestionOf D u)).postprocess
    46	                        (directLdPointValuesOrZero D)).effect outcome) 1)
    47	                  (fun u outcome =>
    48	                    heteroKron 1
    49	                      ((GB.postprocess (evalDirectPolyTupleAt u)).effect outcome))
    50	                  S.ψ ≤ deltaLd a b ε D.q D.m D.d D.k ∧
    51	              consistencyDefect
    52	                  (uniformDistribution (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D))
    53	                  (fun u outcome =>
    54	                    heteroKron
    55	                      ((GA.postprocess (evalDirectPolyTupleAt u)).effect outcome) 1)
    56	                  (fun u outcome =>
    57	                    heteroKron 1
    58	                      (((S.B (directLdPointQuestionOf D u)).postprocess
    59	                        (directLdPointValuesOrZero D)).effect outcome))
    60	                  S.ψ ≤ deltaLd a b ε D.q D.m D.d D.k ∧
    61	              consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution Unit)
    62	                  (fun _ g => heteroKron (GA.effect g) 1)
    63	                  (fun _ g => heteroKron 1 (GB.effect g))
    64	                  S.ψ ≤ deltaLd a b ε D.q D.m D.d D.k := by
    65	  sorry

    67	end

 "body": "<!-- mipstarre-issue-key: stage43-direct-low-degree-game-value -->
### Motivation

- Parent: #47.
- Depends only on the structural split in #67 and may proceed in parallel with
  the geometry packet #71 once that split lands.
- The direct low-degree game has nine uniformly sampled ordered type branches,
  while the mature low-degree-test hypothesis weights the point/point branch by
  `1 / 3` and each of the four line/point orientations by `1 / 6`.
- Isolating the resulting rejection calculus gives the later native-LDT adapter
  its exact scalar error budget without changing the final soundness theorem or
  introducing a bridge hypothesis.
- Sources: QPBT paper
  `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:274-392`,
  blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:87-121`, and the mature
  LDT strategy interface in
  `references/ldt-paper/test_definition.tex:130-151` and
  `MIPStarRE/LDT/Test/StrategyBiProj/Measurements.lean:455-528`.

### Target

Create only
`MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/DirectLowDegree/GameValue.lean`, importing
`MIPStarRE.QPBT.Combining.DirectLowDegree.Game`.

Define the private Born weight of an answer pair for a fixed direct question
pair, then add these public quantities and lemmas with the stated signatures:

```lean
noncomputable def directLdBranchRejectionProbability
    (D : DirectLdParams) (S : Strategy (directLdGame D))
    (types : LdType × LdType) : ℝ

noncomputable def directLdRejectionProbability
    (D : DirectLdParams) (S : Strategy (directLdGame D)) : ℝ

noncomputable def directLdLdtWeightedFailureProbability
    (D : DirectLdParams) (S : Strategy (directLdGame D)) : ℝ

theorem directLdBranchRejectionProbability_nonneg
    (D : DirectLdParams) (S : Strategy (directLdGame D))
    (types : LdType × LdType) :
    0 ≤ directLdBranchRejectionProbability D S types

theorem directLdRejectionProbability_eq_one_sub_value
    (D : DirectLdParams) (S : Strategy (directLdGame D)) :
    directLdRejectionProbability D S = 1 - S.value

theorem directLdLdtWeightedFailureProbability_le_three_mul_rejection
    (D : DirectLdParams) (S : Strategy (directLdGame D)) :
    directLdLdtWeightedFailureProbability D S ≤
      3 * directLdRejectionProbability D S

theorem directLdLdtWeightedFailureProbability_le_three_mul_error
    (D : DirectLdParams) (S : Strategy (directLdGame D))
    (ε : ℝ) (hwin : 1 - ε ≤ S.value) :
    directLdLdtWeightedFailureProbability D S ≤ 3 * ε
```

`directLdBranchRejectionProbability D S types` is the uniform average over
`DirectLdSpace D` of the Born weights of rejected answer pairs for the fixed
ordered type pair. `directLdRejectionProbability` is its uniform average over
`LdType × LdType`. If `B` abbreviates the branch probability, define the
mature-LDT-weighted failure probability as

```text
((B (aline, point) + B (point, aline)) / 2
  + B (point, point)
  + (B (dline, point) + B (point, dline)) / 2) / 3.
```

Use the existing game verifier and strategy measurements; do not restate the
acceptance predicate or add a second strategy representation.

### Proof order

1. Prove the private answer-pair Born weight is nonnegative from positivity of
   the measurement effects and their tensor product.
2. Sum the answer-pair weights to one using measurement completeness and the
   strategy state's normalization.
3. Partition answer pairs into accepted and rejected outcomes for each fixed
   question and type pair.
4. Use the existing finite-distribution averaging API, including uniform
   product averaging, to identify total rejection with `1 - S.value`.
5. Enumerate the nine ordered `LdType` branches. Nonnegativity of the four
   branches omitted by the mature LDT expression gives the exact factor-three
   inequality.
6. Combine the identity with `hwin` to obtain the `3 * ε` bound.

No projectivity hypothesis is needed for this probability calculation.

### Statement integrity

This packet proves formalization-only consequences of the already defined
direct game. The factor three records the exact comparison between the game's
nine uniform ordered type branches and the five mature-LDT branches; it is not
a new source theorem or a weakened error estimate. The assumptions and
conclusions add no bridge, residual package, or producer input. Verdict:
source-faithful auxiliary calculus with no extra mathematical assumptions and
no weakened conclusion. Do not add blueprint `\lean` or `\leanok` tags.

The mature `LDT.Test.mainFormal` theorem supplies scalar acceptance bounds; it
does not by itself construct the arbitrary-`D.k` joint measurement needed by
`exists_direct_ld_soundness`. This issue must stop before that adapter and must
not hide the missing construction behind a hypothesis.

### Ownership and non-goals

- Own only the new `DirectLowDegree/GameValue.lean` file.
- Do not edit `Geometry.lean`, `Game.lean`, `Soundness.lean`, the
  `DirectLowDegree.lean` facade, `MIPStarRE/QPBT.lean`, blueprint files, or
  paper-gap notes.
- Keep implementation helpers private; do not widen the shared game,
  distribution, measurement, or LDT APIs.
- Do not construct a native LDT strategy, prove simultaneous soundness, alter
  `exists_direct_ld_soundness`, or introduce a conditional bridge theorem.
- Do not depend on the geometry proofs in #71. Keep the packet bounded to the
  rejection/value calculation; expected size is at most about 250 lines.

### Acceptance

- `lake env lean MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/DirectLowDegree/GameValue.lean`
  succeeds without linter warnings.
- The new file contains no `sorry`, `admit`, new axiom, prohibited bypass, or
  conclusion-shaped assumption.
- All declarations above have exactly the stated signatures and the definitions
  have the stated probability semantics.
- Only `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/DirectLowDegree/GameValue.lean` differs; the
  existing direct-soundness proof debt and all public signatures remain
  unchanged.
- `lake build`, `git diff --check`, exact-head CI, and independent review pass.

 "body": "<!-- mipstarre-issue-key: stage43-direct-low-degree-geometry -->\n### Motivation\n\n- Parent: #47.\n- Depends on the structural split in #67.\n- The direct-index game already defines the repaired axis and diagonal sampling\n  laws, but its five elementary geometry statements remain admitted.\n- These statements are the direct-index counterparts of `lem:alnf` and\n  `lem:dlnf`, paper\n  `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:243-272`\n  and blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:61-85`.\n- Proving them unlocks the native-LDT adapter without restoring the invalid\n  dimension-divisibility assumption.\n\n### Targets\n\nIn `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/DirectLowDegree/Geometry.lean`, replace only the\nexisting proofs of:\n\n- `directALinePointDist_point_index_marginal_uniform`\n- `directALinePointDist_mem_line`\n- `directDLinePointDist_point_index_marginal_uniform`\n- `directDLinePointDist_mem_line`\n- `directDLinePointDist_prefix_zero`\n\nPreserve every declaration name, argument, result type, and docstring.\n\n### Proof order\n\n1. Add only private, file-local helpers needed for finite-distribution\n   extensionality, composition of probability-preserving pushforwards, and\n   uniform projection along an explicit finite equivalence.\n2. Exhibit `DirectLdSpace D` as both point times index/direction and index times\n   point/direction. Use those equivalences and Mathlib's uniform-PMF transport\n   and product results to prove both point/index marginal conjunctions.\n3. Prove the private fact `u \u2208 linePoints (lineRepMap v u) v`. Use\n   `Submodule.sub_projection_mem` for the canonical complementary projection,\n   then `Submodule.mem_span_singleton` to obtain the line parameter.\n4. Unpack membership in each mapped uniform support with\n   `Distribution.map_support`; apply the geometric fact to prove both incidence\n   statements.\n5. Unpack diagonal support in the same way and apply\n   `DirectLineDesc.diagonal_prefix_zero` for the prefix-zero statement.\n\nAll five proof shapes have been prototyped successfully. Do not use the\nadmitted non-direct analogues in `Test/LowDegreeGameTheorems.lean` as proof\nshortcuts.\n\n### Statement integrity\n\nThe paper samples a uniform point and a uniform axis or prefix index, with the\ndiagonal direction zero below that index. `D : DirectLdParams` supplies the\nfinite nonempty types used by the definitions. The Lean conclusions are\nexactly the uniform point/index marginals, line incidence, and diagonal\nprefix-zero property for the direct-index repair. Verdict: faithful\ndirect-index encoding with ambient parameter fields; no extra proof\nassumptions, weakened conclusions, or changed quantifiers. These are\nformalization auxiliaries, not replacements for the source-labelled blueprint\ndeclarations.\n\nThe completed proofs will still inherit existing construction debt from\n`exists_fixed_field_model` and, for incidence, from\n`isCompl_registerSubmodule_canonicalComplement`. Do not claim axiom-clean\nclosure or add an `**Unfaithful:**` marker: these are visible source-faithful\nconstruction obligations, not new load-bearing hypotheses.\n\n### Ownership and non-goals\n\n- Own only `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/DirectLowDegree/Geometry.lean`.\n- Keep helpers private; do not widen shared Distribution, PMF, line, or\n  subspace APIs.\n- Do not edit `Game.lean`, `Soundness.lean`, the facade,\n  `MIPStarRE/QPBT.lean`, `Witnesses.lean`, or `Apply.lean`.\n- Do not change the blueprint, paper-gap notes, definitions, imports, or\n  theorem signatures.\n- Do not address direct-game rejection calculus, native-strategy construction,\n  error bounds, simultaneous encoding, or soundness.\n- Keep the implementation bounded to the five proofs and necessary private\n  helpers; expected size is about 150-200 changed lines.\n\n### Acceptance\n\n- Direct-check `Geometry.lean`, `Game.lean`, `Soundness.lean`, the facade, and\n  `Combining/Witnesses.lean`.\n- `Geometry.lean` has no `sorry`, `admit`, new axiom, prohibited bypass, or\n  linter warning.\n- The complete direct-low-degree surface has exactly one remaining `sorry`, in\n  `Soundness.lean`.\n- The five public signatures are unchanged and no file outside\n  `Geometry.lean` differs.\n- `lake build`, `git diff --check`, exact-head CI, and independent review pass.\n\n---\nStage 4.3 mathematics packet under #47; blocked only by #67.",

 "body": "<!-- mipstarre-issue-key: qpbt-stage43-magic-square-perfect-strategy -->
### Motivation

Prove the converse Magic Square construction `thm:ms-from-ac`: any exact
anticommuting pair of consistent binary projective measurements extends to a
value-one SPCC Magic Square strategy. The canonical statement and full
operator-table proof are
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:654-878`;
the matched blueprint node is
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:255-286`.

### Target

After the Magic Square foundation/split packet #75, prove only the existing
declaration `MIPStarRE.QPBT.exists_ms_perfect_strategy_of_anticommuting` in
`MIPStarRE/QPBT/Test/MagicSquareTheorems/PerfectStrategy.lean`, preserving its
signature verbatim.

In particular preserve arbitrary finite nonempty `ι`, the hypotheses `hA`,
`hB`, `hcA`, `hcB`, and `hac`, and every exact conclusion: `S.ι = ι × ZMod 2`,
`S.IsSPCC`, value `1`, state `msPerfectState ι`, and the
variable-0/variable-4 effect embeddings.

### Dependencies

- Base on merged #75.
- Base on #64 for the clean `eprState_norm` theorem used to normalize
  `msPerfectState`.
- This packet is independent of #49, #68, the rigidity packet, #69, and
  encoding/decoding. If #68 is already merged, reuse a directly applicable
  binary identity only when it avoids local duplication; do not make it a hard
  dependency or introduce type-reindexing infrastructure merely to use it.

### Proof route

1. From `hA` and `hB`, establish locally that `obsOf A` and `obsOf B` are
   Hermitian involutions and recover each binary effect as
   `(1 ± obsOf _)/2`.
2. Define the single-qubit `X` and `Z` observables on `ZMod 2` from the existing
   concrete Pauli matrices, or equivalent private entrywise definitions. Prove
   their Hermiticity, involution, exact anticommutation, and consistency on
   `eprState (ZMod 2)` by finite extensional calculation.
3. Define the nine cell observables exactly as the paper's table:

   `OA⊗I, I⊗X, OA⊗X; I⊗Z, OB⊗I, OB⊗Z; OA⊗Z, OB⊗X, OA*OB⊗Z*X`.

4. Use `hac` and `XZ = -ZX` to prove that the bottom-right cell is Hermitian
   and squares to one. Prove pairwise commutation within all six rows/columns,
   and that their products are `I` except for the final column, whose product
   is `-I`.
5. Turn each Hermitian involution into its binary PVM. For variable questions,
   embed `.bit b` and assign zero to `.triple _`.
6. For each constraint, define the joint triple PVM by multiplying the three
   commuting cell projections. Embed `.triple beta` and assign zero to `.bit
   _`; prove positivity, completeness, orthogonality, and idempotence from
   pairwise commutation.
7. Assemble the symmetric strategy on local carrier `ι × ZMod 2`, so the
   equality witness is `rfl`; normalize and swap the state `reindexState
   prodShuffle (vecTensor (eprState ι) (eprState (ZMod 2)))` using #64 and
   tensor/reindex norm laws.
8. Prove SPCC in order: projectivity for both question forms, cell/constraint
   consistency on the tensor EPR state, then support-wise commutation for each
   constraint-variable incidence.
9. Prove value one supportwise: parity follows from the six row/column product
   identities and answer consistency follows from the joint measurement
   marginal. Sum accepted outcomes to one using measurement completeness and
   `msGame.μ_prob`.
10. Finish the exact variable-0 and variable-4 effect equalities by unfolding
    the construction; do not replace them with observable-only equalities.

Keep all operator-table, reflection-to-PVM, and finite-index lemmas private or
file-local.

### Statement integrity

Paper assumptions: two binary PVMs on `(ℂ^q)^{⊗n}`, EPR consistency, and
exact observable anticommutation. Lean assumptions: the same conditions on an
arbitrary finite nonempty local carrier `ι`; `Fintype`, `DecidableEq`, and
`Nonempty` are representation boundary hypotheses. Paper conclusion: symmetric
value-one SPCC strategy on the original EPR system tensored with one EPR pair,
embedding `A` at variable 1 and `B` at variable 5. Lean conclusion is identical
after zero-based labels 0 and 4 and explicit type transport `hι`. Verdict:
faithful carrier-generalized encoding, no extra load-bearing assumption and no
weakened conclusion.

### Ownership and non-goals

Own only
`MIPStarRE/QPBT/Test/MagicSquareTheorems/PerfectStrategy.lean` after the split.
Do not touch `MagicSquare.lean`, `MagicSquareTheorems.lean` (the rigidity
owner/facade), its `Basic.lean`, Pauli or distance files, blueprint, re-exports,
or `Completeness.lean`.

Do not change the theorem signature, restrict `ι` to a field model, weaken
`IsSPCC`, value, state, or effect equalities, postulate a joint-measurement API,
or add public mechanisms, bridge assumptions, conditional helpers, axioms, or
new proof holes.

### Acceptance

- `exists_ms_perfect_strategy_of_anticommuting` is complete with its exact
  existing signature.
- Its `#print axioms` output contains no `sorryAx`.
- The owned file contains no `sorry`, `admit`, axiom, or prohibited bypass.
- The statement-integrity audit records the zero-based indices, carrier
  generalization, and exact state/effect conclusions.
- The focused file, `Test/Completeness.lean`, and `MIPStarRE/QPBT.lean`
  type-check; full build, declaration/blueprint checks, diff check, exact-head
  CI, and independent review pass.
- No blueprint or re-export edit is needed.

---
Stage 4.3 proof packet under #47.

  1065	the original test, is essential for our applications to
  1066	self-testing. Ultimately we will require the provers to succeed in a linearity test performed in either of two mutually incompatible bases (e.g. the $X$ and $Z$ bases). Two provers

   869	between measurements that has been frequently used in the context of

   875	$$ \Drho(S, T) := \sqrt{\Trho\big( (S-T)^\dagger(S-T)\rho\big)}.$$

   877	summing the state-dependent distance between the square roots of the POVM elements.

   880	$\ket{\psi}$ be a quantum state. Then the state-dependent distance between the POVMs
   881	$M$ and $N$ on $\rho$ is denoted as $\Drho(\sqrt{M}, \sqrt{N})$ and

    33	/-- Identify the direct extended game's scalar field with the Pauli scalar
    34	field.  Both are selected by `fixedFieldModel`; only their proof argument for
    35	admissibility differs. -/
    36	noncomputable def extendedDirectScalarEquiv (P : AdmissibleParams) :
    37	    DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd ≃+* PauliScalar P := by
    38	  have h : P.extendedDirectLd.hq = P.hq := Subsingleton.elim _ _
    39	  cases h
    40	  exact RingEquiv.refl _
    41	
    42	/-- Transport an extended direct point into the canonical Pauli scalar field. -/
    43	def directPointToPauli (P : AdmissibleParams)
    44	    (u : Fin P.extendedDirectLd.m -> DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd) :
    45	    Fin (2 * P.m + 2) -> PauliScalar P :=
    46	  fun i => extendedDirectScalarEquiv P (u i)

    50	/-- A finite code for directly indexed lines, omitting only proof fields. -/
    51	private abbrev DirectLineDescCode (D : DirectLdParams) :=
    52	  ((Fin D.m -> DirectScalarQ D) × Fin D.m) ⊕
    53	    ((Fin D.m -> DirectScalarQ D) × Fin D.m ×
    54	      (Fin D.m -> DirectScalarQ D))
    55	
    56	/-- Encode a directly indexed line by its tag and mathematical data. -/
    57	private def directLineDescCode (D : DirectLdParams) :
    58	    DirectLineDesc D -> DirectLineDescCode D
    59	  | .axis base index _ => .inl (base, index)
    60	  | .diagonal base index direction _ _ => .inr (base, index, direction)
    61	
    62	/-- The direct-line code is injective by proof irrelevance. -/
    63	private theorem directLineDescCode_injective (D : DirectLdParams) :
    64	    Function.Injective (directLineDescCode D) := by
    65	  intro line line' h
    66	  cases line with
    67	  | axis base index baseFixed =>
    68	      cases line' with
    69	      | axis base' index' baseFixed' =>
    70	          simp only [directLineDescCode, Sum.inl.injEq, Prod.mk.injEq] at h
    71	          rcases h with ⟨rfl, rfl⟩
    72	          rfl
    73	      | diagonal => simp [directLineDescCode] at h
    74	  | diagonal base index direction baseFixed prefixZero =>
    75	      cases line' with
    76	      | axis => simp [directLineDescCode] at h
    77	      | diagonal base' index' direction' baseFixed' prefixZero' =>
    78	          simp only [directLineDescCode, Sum.inr.injEq, Prod.mk.injEq] at h
    79	          rcases h with ⟨rfl, rfl, rfl⟩
    80	          rfl

    82	/-- Directly indexed line descriptions form a finite type. -/
    83	noncomputable instance directLineDescFintype (D : DirectLdParams) :
    84	    Fintype (DirectLineDesc D) :=
    85	  Fintype.ofInjective (directLineDescCode D) (directLineDescCode_injective D)

    92	structure CombinedPointsWitness {P : AdmissibleParams} {ε : ℝ}

    94	  /-- The complete joint measurement on each player's expanded local space. -/

    96	    (Fin P.m -> PauliScalar P) ->
    97	    (Fin P.m -> PauliScalar P) ->
    98	    Measurement (PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P) (S.ExpandedLocalSpace side)
    99	  /-- Every joint point measurement is projective. -/

   101	  /-- Joint point measurements agree across every directed opposite placement. -/
   102	  self_consistent : ∀ p1 p2 : Placement, p1.IsOpposite p2 ->
   103	    opFamilyDistSq

   105	        ((Fin P.m -> PauliScalar P) × (Fin P.m -> PauliScalar P)))
   106	      (fun xz ab => S.place p1 ((Q p1.side xz.1 xz.2).effect ab))
   107	      (fun xz ab => S.place p2 ((Q p2.side xz.1 xz.2).effect ab))

   114	      (fun xz ab => S.place p1 ((Q p1.side xz.1 xz.2).effect ab))

   118	      S.psiHat <= δ

   123	        ((Fin P.m -> PauliScalar P) × (Fin P.m -> PauliScalar P)))
   124	      (fun xz ab => S.place p1 ((Q p1.side xz.1 xz.2).effect ab))

   127	          (S.pointMeasExp p2.side .X xz.1).effect ab.1))

   168	/-- A tuple consisting of an extended line and its projected X and Z lines. -/
   169	abbrev SubLineTriple (P : AdmissibleParams) :=
   170	  DirectLineDesc P.extendedDirectLd ×
   171	    (LineDesc P.toLdParams × LineDesc P.toLdParams)

   173	/-- An extended line tuple together with a point sampled uniformly on it. -/
   174	abbrev SubLinePointSample (P : AdmissibleParams) :=
   175	  SubLineTriple P ×

   180	abbrev SubLineComponent (P : AdmissibleParams) :=

   183	/-- Select the restricted line-point distribution of a given kind and index. -/
   184	noncomputable def restrictedLinePointDist (P : AdmissibleParams)
   185	    (kind : LineKind) (i : Fin P.m) :
   186	    Distribution (LineDesc P.toLdParams × (Fin P.m -> PauliScalar P)) :=

   189	  | .diagonal => restrictedDLineDist P.toLdParams i

   191	/-- Sample a subline tuple and then a uniform affine parameter on its
   192	extended line. -/
   193	noncomputable def subLinePointDist (P : AdmissibleParams)
   194	    (D : Distribution (SubLineTriple P)) :
   195	    Distribution (SubLinePointSample P) :=
   196	  (Distribution.prod D
   197	    (uniformDistribution (DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd))).map fun sample =>

   206	/-- Retain the projected line pair and the Z projection of an extended point. -/

   208	    (LineDesc P.toLdParams × LineDesc P.toLdParams) ×
   209	      (Fin P.m -> PauliScalar P) :=
   210	  (sample.1.2, projZ (directPointToPauli P sample.2))

   213	noncomputable def subLineXComponentDist (P : AdmissibleParams)

   215	    Distribution

   217	        (Fin P.m -> PauliScalar P)) :=

    36	  AnswerB : Type
    37	  [questionAFintype : Fintype QuestionA]

    40	  [answerBFintype : Fintype AnswerB]

    53	/--
    54	The marginal of a joint POVM obtained by post-processing its answer pair.  This

    56	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:8-26`; the post-processing operation

    60	noncomputable def marginalLeft {α β d : Type*}

    88	structure Strategy (G : Game) where
    89	  ιA : Type
    90	  ιB : Type
    91	  [ιAFintype : Fintype ιA]
    92	  [ιBFintype : Fintype ιB]
    93	  [ιADecidableEq : DecidableEq ιA]
    94	  [ιBDecidableEq : DecidableEq ιB]
    95	  ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB)
    96	  ψ_norm : ‖ψ‖ = 1
    97	  A : G.QuestionA → Measurement G.AnswerA ιA
    98	  B : G.QuestionB → Measurement G.AnswerB ιB

   100	attribute [instance] Strategy.ιAFintype Strategy.ιBFintype
   101	  Strategy.ιADecidableEq Strategy.ιBDecidableEq
   102	
   103	/-- The rectangular tensor placement used in strategy probabilities.  This is
   104	the finite-matrix realization of `def:tensor-product-strategy`, blueprint
   105	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:61-69`; paper origin
   106	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:26-38`.
   107	-/
   108	def heteroKron {ιA ιB : Type*} (A : Op ιA) (B : Op ιB) : Op (ιA × ιB) :=
   109	  Matrix.kronecker A B
   110	
   111	/- The Euclidean linear map is the shared action used by the value and distance
   112	functionals.  Keeping it at the Euclidean-space level avoids accidentally
   113	using the function-space supremum norm of `Matrix.mulVec`. -/
   114	/-- Apply a finite matrix to a Euclidean-space state.  This is the Hilbert-space
   115	action underlying `def:tensor-product-value`, paper
   116	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:219-271`. -/
   117	noncomputable def applyOperatorToState {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   118	    (M : Op ι) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι :=
   119	  Matrix.toEuclideanLin M ψ
   120	
   121	/-- The Born weight of an answer pair for a strategy.  Lean-only support for
   122	`def:tensor-product-value`, blueprint `ch12_qpbt_games.tex:71-82`, paper
   123	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:219-271`. -/
   124	private noncomputable def outcomeWeight {G : Game} (S : Strategy G)
   125	    (x : G.QuestionA) (y : G.QuestionB) (a : G.AnswerA) (b : G.AnswerB) : ℝ :=
   126	  let M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (S.ιA × S.ιB) :=
   127	    heteroKron ((S.A x).effect a) ((S.B y).effect b)
   128	  let acted := applyOperatorToState M S.ψ
   129	  (inner ℂ S.ψ acted).re
   130	
   131	/--
   132	The tensor-product value, expressed as the distribution average of the Born
   133	probabilities.  This is `def:tensor-product-value` in
   134	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:71-82`, with paper origin
   135	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:40-57`.
   136	-/
   137	noncomputable def Strategy.value {G : Game} (S : Strategy G) : ℝ :=
   138	  avgOver G.μ (fun xy =>
   139	    ∑ a : G.AnswerA, ∑ b : G.AnswerB,
   140	      if G.decide xy.1 xy.2 a b then outcomeWeight S xy.1 xy.2 a b else 0)
   141	
   142	/--
   143	The tensor-product game value as a conditional supremum over all finite
   144	strategies.  The `sSup (Set.range ...)` form is the csSup formulation requested
   145	for `def:tensor-product-value`, blueprint
   146	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:71-82`, paper origin
   147	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:40-57`; attainment is
   148	intentionally not asserted here.
   149	-/
   150	noncomputable def Game.value (G : Game) : ℝ :=
   151	  sSup (Set.range (fun S : Strategy G => S.value))
   152

    28	structure SymmetricGame where
    29	  Question : Type
    30	  Answer : Type
    31	  [questionFintype : Fintype Question]
    32	  [answerFintype : Fintype Answer]
    33	  [questionDecidableEq : DecidableEq Question]
    34	  [answerDecidableEq : DecidableEq Answer]
    35	  μ : Distribution (Question × Question)
    36	  μ_prob : μ.IsProbability
    37	  μ_symm : ∀ x y, μ.weight (x, y) = μ.weight (y, x)

    58	The two local spaces and measurement families are identified, as in the source

    60	structure SymmetricStrategy (G : SymmetricGame) where
    61	  ι : Type
    62	  [ιFintype : Fintype ι]
    63	  [ιDecidableEq : DecidableEq ι]

    65	  ψ_norm : ‖ψ‖ = 1
    66	  ψ_swap : reindexState (Equiv.prodComm ι ι) ψ = ψ
    67	  M : G.Question → Measurement G.Answer ι
    68	
    69	attribute [instance] SymmetricStrategy.ιFintype SymmetricStrategy.ιDecidableEq
    70	
    71	/-- Regard a symmetric strategy as a strategy using the same local space and
    72	measurement family for both players; `def:symmetric-game`, blueprint
    73	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:100-109`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:74-92`. -/
    74	def SymmetricStrategy.toStrategy {G : SymmetricGame} (S : SymmetricStrategy G) :

    83	/-- Common-space commutation from `def:comm-strategy`, blueprint
    84	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:141-150`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:132-142`. -/
    85	def IsCommutingOn {X Y α β ι : Type*}
    86	    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype Y] [DecidableEq Y]
    87	    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Fintype β]
    88	    [DecidableEq β] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    89	    (μ : Distribution (X × Y)) (A : X → Measurement α ι)
    90	    (B : Y → Measurement β ι) : Prop :=
    91	  ∀ x y, 0 < μ.weight (x, y) → ∀ a b, Commute ((A x).effect a) ((B y).effect b)

    93	private def transportOp {d₁ d₂ : Type u} (h : d₁ = d₂) (M : Op d₂) : Op d₁ :=

    96	/-- Transported common-space form of `def:comm-strategy`, blueprint

    98	def Strategy.IsCommuting {G : Game} (S : Strategy G) (hι : S.ιA = S.ιB) : Prop :=
    99	  ∀ x y, 0 < G.μ.weight (x, y) → ∀ a b,

   112	def IsConsistentStrategyOn {X Y α β ι : Type*}
   113	    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype Y] [DecidableEq Y]
   114	    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Fintype β] [DecidableEq β]
   115	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   116	    (A : X → Measurement α ι) (B : Y → Measurement β ι)
   117	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ι × ι)) : Prop :=
   118	  (∀ x, MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsConsistentOn (A x) ψ) ∧
   119	    ∀ y, MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsConsistentOn (B y) ψ

   122	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:169-174`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:162-174`. -/
   123	def SymmetricStrategy.IsConsistent {G : SymmetricGame}
   124	    (S : SymmetricStrategy G) : Prop :=

   132	    (A : G.QuestionA → Measurement G.AnswerA ι)
   133	    (B : G.QuestionB → Measurement G.AnswerB ι)
   134	  (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ι × ι)) : Prop :=
   135	  (∀ x, MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (A x)) ∧

Preserve the source statements and the canonical fixed-field model.\n\n### Mathematical source\n\n- Primary paper mirrors: `references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex`,\n  `05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex`, `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex`,\n  `07_types.tex`, and `08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex`.\n- Blueprint: `blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex` through\n  `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex`.\n- Binding implementation contract:\n  `local/briefs/42-residual-brief.md`, including its 2026-09-02 operator adjudication.\n\n### Target Lean declarations\n\nAdd the residual algebra, game-calculus, low-degree, Magic Square, completeness,\nqubit-form, and canonical-parameter modules listed in the brief. The residual wave owns\nthe canonical-model decoding/binary-representation views, `SymmetricGame`, and the\nshared error/distribution leaf infrastructure. It also owns `Strategy.IsProjective`,\nstate-dependent consistency, the original `linePointDist`, `opDistSq`, and the neutral\nstate helpers relocated from `Test/Soundness.lean`, plus `vecTensor` and `prodShuffle`.\nIt owns the generic `Fintype`\ninstance for bounded `polyFunc`, which is required by `PolyMeas` and later consumed by\nch15; the existing subtype `DecidableEq` is reused.\n\n### Mathematical dependencies\n\n- PR #5 must merge before implementation begins.\n- Tracking issue #1.\n- Existing paper-gap notes for symmetrization and LDT dimension divisibility.\n\n### Implementation constraints\n\n- Remove all stale `FieldModel` assumptions; use `P.model` and `L.model`.\n- Move `conjIsometry`, `reindexState`, and `isometryTensor` to the neutral\n  `MIPStarRE/QPBT/State.lean` leaf; no residual module may import `Test/Soundness.lean`.\n  Generalize `isometryTensor` to arbitrary finite codomain index types, and define real\n  `vecTensor` and `prodShuffle` helpers in the same leaf.\n- Do not introduce `SelfDualNormalRep` or another basis/model input.\n- Keep decoding, basis-coordinate, trace/dot-product, and Magic Square\n  anticommutation source nodes generic; add canonical `FixedFieldModel`\n  specializations for QPBT consumers.\n- Implement the tagged canonical `LineDesc`, the source-general `PolyMeasFamily`, and\n  the transported common-index `AreCloseStrategies` contract from the adjudication.\n- State the unrestricted twisted-commutation and cancellation nodes over a general prime\n  with `MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.ffChar`. Keep characteristic-two QPBT results as\n  separately named specializations and never link them as the source theorems. Create\n  `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_characteristic-two-pauli-scope.tex` and cite it from the scoped\n  consumer declarations.\n- Define `PolyMeas` over the actual bounded `polyFunc` subtype. Provide a generic\n  `Fintype` instance with the existing `Module.finite_of_finite` and\n  `Fintype.ofFinite` route; reuse the existing subtype `DecidableEq`. No coefficient\n  equivalence or competing equality instance is needed. Declare dependent aliases\n  noncomputable.\n- Keep `deltaLd` distinct from `deltaQld`.\n- Give the close-strategy value theorem the source's separate transported state-equality\n  hypothesis; general strategy closeness alone is insufficient.\n- Quantify the constants in Magic Square rigidity and close-strategy value stability\n  before all strategies and error parameters. Do the same for commutation analysis and\n  the low-degree sandwich bound. Preserve the `0 \u2264 \u03b5` boundary in the qubit soundness\n  corollary, use `P.model.basisDim`, and add no field-model or basis argument.\n- Serialize the aggregate `MIPStarRE/QPBT.lean` import edit at integration time.\n\n### Acceptance criteria\n\n- Every in-scope declaration exists and every definition body is real.\n- Edited Lean files type-check; only explicitly tracked Stage 4.2 proof `sorry`s remain.\n- Blueprint declarations and direct `\\uses` metadata are synchronized faithfully.\n- `lake build`, blueprint rendering, declaration checking, and local CI pass on the\n  exact PR head; a separate reviewer approves it.\n\n### Tracking issue\n\n#1\n",

    98	\begin{definition}[General projective strategy]
    99	A \emph{projective strategy} for the $(m,q, d)$-low individual degree test
   100	is a tuple $(\psi, A^{\mathrm{A}},B^{\mathrm{A}},L^{\mathrm{A}},A^{\mathrm{B}},B^{\mathrm{B}},L^{\mathrm{B}})$ defined as follows.
   101	\begin{itemize}
   102	\item[$\circ$] $\ket{\psi} \in \calH_{\mathrm{A}} \ot \calH_{\mathrm{B}}$ is a bipartite state.

   104	Furthermore, for each~$w \in \{\mathrm{A}, \mathrm{B}\}$:

   106	\item[$\circ$] $A^{w} = \{A^{w,u}_a\}$ contains a matrix for each $u \in \F_q^m$ and $a \in \F_q$.
   107				For each $u$, $A^{w,u}$ is a projective measurement on~$\calH_{w}$.
   108	\item[$\circ$] $B^{w} = \{B^{w,\ell}_f\}$ contains a matrix for each axis-parallel line~$\ell$ in $\F_q^m$
   109				and univariate degree-$d$ polynomial $f:\ell\rightarrow \F_q$.
   110				For each $\ell$, $B^{w,\ell}$ is a projective measurement on~$\calH_{w}$.
   111	\item[$\circ$] $L^w = \{L^{w,\ell}_f\}$ contains a matrix for each line~$\ell$ in $\F_q^m$
   112				and univariate degree-$md$ polynomial $f:\ell\rightarrow \F_q$.
   113				For each $\ell$, $L^{w,\ell}$ is a projective measurement on~$\calH_{w}$.
   114	\end{itemize}
   115	\end{definition}

   118	Throughout this work, we will only consider projective strategies.

   121	In addition, we will spend the vast majority of this work dealing solely with symmetric strategies, as they are notationally simpler to work with.
   122	Much of this work will focus on proving~\Cref{thm:main-induction},
   123	a variant of our main theorem for symmetric strategies.
   124	Our main theorem for general strategies, \Cref{thm:main-formal} below, will be proven in \Cref{sec:induction} by a standard reduction to the symmetric case.
   125	We will only see these more cumbersome-to-write general strategies
   126	in this section, where we state \Cref{thm:main-formal},
   127	and in \Cref{sec:induction}, where we carry out the reduction.
   128	\end{remark}
   129	
   130	\begin{definition}[Good strategy]
   131	A strategy is $(\eps, \delta, \gamma)$-good if it
   132	passes the axis-parallel lines test with probability at least $1-\eps$,
   133	the self consistency test with probability at least~$1-\delta$,
   134	and the diagonal lines test with probability at least~$1-\gamma$.
   135	\end{definition}
   136	
   137	\begin{remark}\label{rem:good-strat-characterization}
   138	Using notation which will be introduced in \Cref{sec:comparing-measurements} below,
   139	a symmetric strategy is $(\eps, \delta, \gamma)$-good
   140	if and only if it satisfies the following three conditions.
   141	For $\bell$ and $\bu$ as in the axis-parallel lines test,
   142	\begin{equation*}
   143	A^u_a \ot I \simeq_{\eps} I \ot B^{\ell}_{[f(u)=a]},
   144	\quad
   145	\text{and}
   146	\quad
   147	A^u_a \ot I \simeq_{\delta} I \ot A^u_a.
   148	\end{equation*}
   149	And for $\bell$ and $\bu$ as in the diagonal lines test,
   150	\begin{equation*}
   151	A^u_a \ot I \simeq_{\gamma} I \ot L^{\ell}_{[f(u)=a]}.
   152	\end{equation*}
   153	\end{remark}
   154	
   155	\begin{notation}\label{not:conditioned-on-last-direction}
   156	Our proof will be via induction,
   157	i.e.\ proving soundness of the $(m+1,q,d)$-low individual degree test
   158	using the soundness of the $(m,q,d)$-low individual degree test.
   159	To do this, we will frequently use the axis-parallel line test in the specific case of $i = m+1$.
   160	Thus, it will be convenient to introduce the following notation.
   161	Let $(\psi, A, B, L)$ be a symmetric strategy for the $(m+1, q, d)$-low individual degree test,
   162	Then for each $u \in \F_q^m$ we will write $B^u_f$ as shorthand for $B^{\ell}_f$,
   163	where $\ell = \{(u, x) \mid x \in \F_q\}$.
   164	For a function $f:\ell \rightarrow \F_q$,
   165	we will also sometimes write $f(x)$ as shorthand for $f(u,x)$.
   166	\end{notation}
   167	
   168	\begin{definition}
   169	Consider the $(m,q,d)$-low individual degree test.
   170	For $j \in \{1, \ldots, m\}$,
   171	we refer to the \emph{$j$-restricted diagonal lines test}
   172	as the diagonal lines test conditioned on $\bi = j$.
   173	For example, in the $m$-restricted diagonal lines test,
   174	the line $\bell$ is simply a uniformly random line in $\F_q^m$.
   175	\end{definition}
   176	
   177	Now we state our main theorem using notation which will be introduced in \Cref{sec:prelims} below.
   178	This the formal version of \Cref{thm:main-informal}.
   179	
   180	\begin{theorem}[Main theorem; quantum soundness of the low individual degree test]\label{thm:main-formal}
   181	  Consider a projective strategy $(\psi, A^{\mathrm{A}},B^{\mathrm{A}},L^{\mathrm{A}},A^{\mathrm{B}},B^{\mathrm{B}},L^{\mathrm{B}})$ 
   182	   which passes the  $(m,q,d)$-low individual degree test with probability at least $1-\eps$.
   183	  Let $k \geq md$ be an integer.
   184	  Let
   185	  \begin{equation*}
   186	  \nu = 100000 k^2m^4 \cdot \Big(\eps^{1/40000} + (d/q)^{1/40000} + e^{-k/(2560000m^2)}\Big).
   187	  \end{equation*}
   188	Then there exists projective measurements $G^{\mathrm{A}}, G^{\mathrm{B}} \in \polymeas{m}{q}{d}$ with the following properties:
   189	\begin{enumerate}
   190	  \item (Consistency with~$A$):  On average over $\bu \sim \F_q^{m}$,
   191		  \begin{align*}
   192		  A^{\mathrm{A},u}_a \otimes I
   193		  	&\simeq_{\nu} I \otimes G^{\mathrm{B}}_{[g(u)=a]},\\
   194		I \otimes A^{\mathrm{B},u}_a
   195		  	&\simeq_{\nu}  G^{\mathrm{A}}_{[g(u)=a]} \ot I.
   196		  \end{align*}
   197	\item (Self-consistency):
   198		\begin{equation*}
   199		G^{\mathrm{A}}_g \ot I \simeq_{\nu} I \ot G^{\mathrm{B}}_g.
   200		\end{equation*}
   201	\end{enumerate}
   202	\end{theorem}
   203	
   204	We note that there is a tradeoff in \Cref{thm:main-formal} specified by the parameter~$k$.
   205	As~$k$ increases, $\nu$'s prefactor $k^2$ increases.
   206	On the other hand, as $k$ increases, the term $e^{- k/(2560000m^2)}$ which also occurs in $\nu$ \emph{decreases}.
   207	Thus, when applying this theorem, one must select~$k$ to balance these competing demands.
   208	Typically, choosing $k = \poly(m)$ should be more than sufficient for applications.
   209	We believe that this parameter~$k$ is an artifact of our proof,
   210	and we hope that it will be removed in the future.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Create a GitHub issue — all that survives of the old ``issues/`` create path.

Before issue 0007 this script allocated a four-digit id from ``issues/.seq``,
wrote ``issues/<id>-<slug>.md`` under a lock, ran a deterministic keyword
classifier against ``local/labels.yml``, then shelled out to a Mathlib scout.
Every one of those responsibilities moved or died:

* the id and the record are GitHub's.  ``gh_common.issue_create`` owns the
  POST, and with ``--key`` it embeds a ``mipstarre-issue-key`` marker so an
  ambiguous create is resolved by adopting the existing issue rather than by
  repeating the mutation (gh_common.py:308-347).
* labels are validated against the *repository's* labels inside that helper,
  so ``local/labels.yml`` is no longer a second source of truth that drifts
  away from what GitHub will accept.
* ``--parent`` is a native sub-issue link (``POST issues/<parent>/sub_issues``),
  not two halves of a hand-maintained relationship.
* classification and scouting are not creation-time concerns.  The old
  deterministic pass existed only to imitate ``classify-outside`` of the
  retired ``.github/workflows/issue-automation.yml``; its LLM sibling was never
  wired.  Nothing here reads a token or calls a model.

No local file is written — not a record, not telemetry: ``dispatch.sh`` owns the
session record.  Fail closed like every other consumer of the GitHub layer: an
API failure exits 2 with the layer's message and leaves nothing behind.

Usage:
    issue_new.py --title "Formalize the Pauli basis test soundness bound" \
                 --body-file /tmp/body.md --label formalization
    issue_new.py --title "Tracking - Pauli basis test" --body "..." \
                 --parent 12 --key qpbt-tracking-pauli
    issue_new.py --help
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import hashlib
import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))
try:
    import gh_common
except ModuleNotFoundError as exc:  # pragma: no cover - defensive
    sys.stderr.write(
        "issue_new.py: cannot import local/bin/gh_common.py, which holds the "
        f"GitHub layer ({exc}).\n"
    )
    raise SystemExit(2)

from wf_util import slugify, BODY_LIMIT, TITLE_LIMIT, LayerError, sanitize  # noqa: E402


def flatten_labels(chunks: list[str]) -> tuple[str, ...]:
    """``--label a,b --label c`` -> ``("a", "b", "c")``, order-preserving; comma
    splitting is kept from the pre-0007 CLI, whose callers pass grouped lists."""
    names: list[str] = []
    for chunk in chunks:
        for name in (part.strip() for part in chunk.split(",")):
            if name and name not in names:
                names.append(name)
    return tuple(names)


def create(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    title = sanitize(args.title, TITLE_LIMIT).strip()
    if not title:
        raise LayerError("--title is empty after sanitization")
    if args.body_file:
        raw = Path(args.body_file).read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    else:
        raw = args.body or ""
    # Bodies round-trip through GitHub, where anyone with read access can quote
    # them back into an agent prompt, so they are untrusted on the way out too
    # (wf_util.sanitize breaks ``` fences and strips control characters).
    body = sanitize(raw, BODY_LIMIT).strip()
    if not body:
        raise LayerError(
            "an issue body is required: pass --body-file PATH or --body TEXT. "
            "The old --template scaffolds are gone; GitHub's issue forms under "
            ".github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/ are where boilerplate belongs now."
        )
    labels = flatten_labels(args.label)

    if args.dry_run:
        sys.stdout.write(
            f"[dry-run] would create issue {title!r} labels={list(labels)} "
            f"parent={args.parent} key={args.key} ({len(body)} body chars)\n"
        )
        return 0

    # Every create is adoption-safe: without an explicit --key the slug plus a
    # short digest of the FULL title is the key, so a retried create adopts —
    # and two distinct titles sharing a truncated slug cannot alias (round 2, F12).
    auto_key = f"{slugify(title)}-{hashlib.sha256(title.encode()).hexdigest()[:8]}"
    number = gh_common.issue_create(
        title, body, labels=labels, parent=args.parent,
        key=args.key or auto_key
    )
    # Bare number on stdout: shell callers capture it with $(...).
    sys.stdout.write(f"{number}\n")
    return 0


def _parse_args(argv: list[str]) -> argparse.Namespace:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        prog="issue_new.py",
        description=__doc__,
        formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter,
    )
    parser.add_argument("--title", required=True,

        sys.stderr.write(f"issue_new.py: {exc}\n")

     5	# The quantum linearity theorem
     6	
     7	This file states the external quantum-linearity result used to combine the
     8	binary observables produced in the point analysis.  The statement uses a
     9	positive semidefinite trace-one operator, and its conclusion adjoins a finite ancillary
    10	space on which the exactly linear observables act.
    11	
    12	## References
    13	
    14	The declaration is `thm:linearity` in
    15	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:82-180`.  The quotation in the
    16	QPBT paper is at
    17	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:713-725`; the
    18	provider is Theorem 10 of Natarajan--Vidick, arXiv:1610.03574.
    19	-/

    22	
    23	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    24	
    25	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    26	open MIPStarRE.Quantum
    27	
    28	noncomputable section
    29	
    30	/-- A binary observable is a Hermitian operator whose square is the identity.
    31	This is the finite-matrix realization of `Obs(H)` in `thm:linearity`, blueprint
    32	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:82-180`, quoted at paper
    33	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:713-725`. -/
    34	def IsBinaryObservable {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    35	    (O : Op ι) : Prop :=
    36	  O.IsHermitian ∧ O * O = 1
    37	
    38	/-- The rank-one density operator associated with an ancillary vector. -/
    39	noncomputable def ancProj {ι : Type} [Fintype ι]
    40	    (v : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : Op ι :=
    41	  let w := (EuclideanSpace.equiv ι ℂ) v

    46	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:82-180`. -/
    47	noncomputable def stateDepDistSq {ι : Type} [Fintype ι]
    48	    (S T ρ : Op ι) : ℝ :=
    49	  (Matrix.trace ((S - T)ᴴ * (S - T) * ρ)).re
    50	
    51	/-- The quantum linearity theorem imported from Natarajan--Vidick.
    52	
    53	The statement is `thm:linearity` in
    54	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:82-145`; the QPBT paper quotes

    68	    (ρ : Op ι) (hρ : ρ.PosSemidef) (htrace : ρ.trace = 1)

    77	            (O pair.1 * O pair.2 * O (pair.1 + pair.2) * ρ)).re)) :

    62	$(q,m,d)$ is admissible when moreover $d \ge 1$ and $m \mid q$, and

    70	  admissible $(q,m,d)$ and every projective strategy for the Pauli basis test

   108	\section{The source assertion and the obstruction}
   109	
   110	We examine the final step of the subsection ``Applying the classical
   111	low-degree test'' in the analysis of the Pauli basis test in the compression
   112	paper of Ji, Natarajan, Vidick, Wright, and Yuen (MIP$^{*}$=RE,
   113	arXiv:2001.04383), whose quantum soundness component builds on the low
   114	individual degree test of \cite{Ji2020LowIndividualDegree}.%
   115	\footnote{Tracked in \localissue{0002}.  In the mirror of the source
   116	consulted here, the polynomial-pair lemma and its proof are at
   117	\path{references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex},
   118	lines~1267--1288; the sub-line lemma is at lines~1063--1116 and the combined
   119	line lemma at lines~1020--1034 of the same file.  The game parametrization
   120	with its divisibility, the index function, the soundness statement with its
   121	proof, and admissibility are at
   122	\path{references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex},
   123	lines~33--35, 214--219, 413--458, and 958--961.}
   124	There, the combined point measurements
   125	$\{\hat Q^{x,z,\alpha,\beta}_c\}$ and combined line measurements
   126	$\{\hat Q^{\ell}_f\}$, indexed by points of $\F_q^{2m+2}$ and lines in
   127	$\F_q^{2m+2}$, are asserted to form a strategy for the classical low
   128	individual degree game with parameters
   129	\[
   130	  \mathsf{ldparams} = (q,\, 2m+2,\, d,\, 1)
   131	  \tag{\path{lem:qld-4-7}}
   132	\]
   133	of value $1 - \delta_{\mathrm{combine}}$, and the quantum soundness theorem
   134	for that game is applied to produce the global polynomial-pair measurement.
   135	The two lemmas feeding this step are stated for the line-point distribution
   136	over $\F_q^{2m+2}$.
   137	
   138	The game, however, is parametrized by tuples $(q,m',d,k)$ with $q$ an
   139	admissible field size \emph{and $m'$ dividing $q$}.  The divisibility is not
   140	incidental: the question distribution is a conditionally linear distribution
   141	in which a uniform seed coordinate $s \in \F_q$, read as an integer in
   142	$\{0,\ldots,q-1\}$, determines the axis or diagonal index through the unique
   143	$\chi(s)$ with
   144	\[
   145	  s = (\chi(s)-1)\,\frac{q}{m'} + r, \qquad 0 \le r < \frac{q}{m'},
   146	  \tag{\path{eq:chi-func}}
   147	\]

   149	size $q/m'$ and the index is uniform.  For $m' \nmid q$ neither the index
   150	function nor the line-point distribution built from it is defined.

   152	Admissibility of $(q,m,d)$ supplies only $m \mid q$.  Since an admissible $q$
   153	is a power of two, $m \mid q$ forces $m = 2^j$.  For $j \ge 1$ the integer
   154	$m+1 \ge 3$ is odd, so $2m+2 = 2(m+1)$ has an odd factor exceeding $1$ and
   155	divides no power of two; for $m = 1$ the condition $4 \mid q$ holds for every
   156	admissible $q$ except $q = 2$.  Thus the instantiation at dimension $2m+2$ is
   157	undefined for every admissible tuple with $m \ge 2$: for instance
   158	$(q,m,d) = (8,2,1)$ is admissible, while $6 \nmid 8$.  The source performs
   159	the instantiation without addressing the divisibility, so its proof route
   160	establishes the polynomial-pair lemma, and with it the soundness theorem for
   161	the Pauli basis test that rests on it, only for $m = 1$ and $q \ge 8$.
   162	
   163	\section{What the cited soundness theorem requires: the import obligations}
   164	\label{sec:import-obligations}
   165	
   166	The quantum soundness theorem for the classical game inherits the constraint
   167	$m' \mid q$ solely because it is stated for the game just described; its
   168	proof fixes an admissible $q$ with $m' \mid q$, asserts that the game with
   169	simultaneity parameter $1$ is \emph{identical} to the two-prover tensor-code
   170	test for the Reed--Solomon tensor code $\mathcal C^{\ot m'}$ of the same
   171	authors' \emph{Quantum soundness of testing tensor codes} (arXiv:2111.08131)
   172	\cite{Ji2021Quantum}, and concludes by Theorem~4.7 there, instantiated with
   173	that theorem's auxiliary integer parameter --- denoted $k$ in that source,
   174	and written $K$ here to avoid clashing with the field exponent and the
   175	simultaneity parameter --- chosen as $(m')^3 d$.  Neither

   177	import carries two verification obligations, which this section details and
   178	which the blueprint's proof node for the soundness statement records as

   180	arise at every dimension, for the $\chi$-based game where it is defined and
   181	equally for the directly indexed variant proposed under the candidate
   182	repairs.
   183	
   184	\paragraph{The cited test.}
   185	In the two-prover tensor-code test (Figures~1 and~2 of
   186	\cite{Ji2021Quantum}; the two-prover strategy format and the goodness
   187	measure are Definitions~4.5 and~4.6 there), the referee performs one of
   188	three subtests with probability $1/3$ each, assigning the two roles of each
   189	subtest to the two provers uniformly at random.  \emph{Axis-parallel lines
   190	test}: sample a uniform point $u \in [n]^{m'}$ and a uniform axis
   191	$j \in \{1,\ldots,m'\}$; send the axis-parallel line $\ell$ through $u$ in
   192	direction $j$ to one prover, who answers a codeword $g \in \mathcal C$;
   193	send $u$ to the other, who answers a field value $a$; accept iff
   194	$g(u_j) = a$.  \emph{Subcube commutation test}: sample
   195	$j \in \{1,\ldots,m'\}$ and a subcube $H \subseteq [n]^{m'}$ by fixing the
   196	last $j-1$ coordinates uniformly; sample $u, v$ independently and uniformly

%----------------------%

We state and analyze a variant of the classic 3-query linearity test of Blum, Luby, and Rubinfeld~\cite{BLR93} (BLR) that can be played with two entangled players. The two-player test is based on the idea of oracularization with a dummy question introduced in~\cite{IKM09}.  Our analysis builds on~\cite{IV12}, who analyze a $3$-player variant. Their proof is an extension of the Fourier-analytic proof due to H{\aa}stad to the matrix-valued setting. We analyze the two-player variant using similar techniques. 

We note that the use of two players, rather than three as in
the original test, is essential for our applications to
self-testing. Ultimately we will require the provers to succeed in a linearity test performed in either of two mutually incompatible bases (e.g. the $X$ and $Z$ bases). Two provers
can achieve this by sharing a maximally entangled state, but there is no {tripartite} state that would allow three entangled provers to obtain consistent answers whenever they measure their share of the state in either the $X$ or the $Z$ basis. (Formulated differently, $\sigma_X\otimes \sigma_X$ and $\sigma_Z\otimes \sigma_Z$ share a common $+1$ eigenvector, the EPR pair; $\sigma_X\otimes \sigma_X \otimes \sigma_X$ and $\sigma_Z\otimes \sigma_Z \otimes \sigma_Z$ do not. This is a manifestation of entanglement monogamy.)

We show the result in two
steps. First we show that any set of quantum observables satisfying
linearity relations approximately in expectation can be ``rounded'' to a
nearby set of observables satisfying these relations exactly. 

\begin{theorem}
  Suppose there exist observables $\{A(a)\}_{a\in
  \{0,1\}^n}$ in $\Obs(\mH)$ acting on a state
  $\rho \in \Density(\mH)$ such that 
	\begin{equation}\label{eq:qblr-0}
	\E_{a, b} \Trho\big( A(a) A(b) A(a+b)\big) \geq 1-\delta.
	\end{equation}
	Then there exists an extended state $\rho' = \rho \otimes
  \proj{\rm{anc}} \in \Density(\mH\otimes \mH')$ and observables $\{\cA(a)\}$ in $\Obs(\mH\otimes\mH')$ such that 
	\begin{equation}\label{eq:qblr-1}
	\cA(a) \cA(b) = \cA(a+b) \quad \forall a, b \in \{0, 1\}^n\qquad \text{and}\qquad \E_a
  \DIS_{\rho'} (\cA(a), A(a))^2 \leq\delta.
	\end{equation}
\label{thm:qblr}
\end{theorem}

Here, and throughout this paper, the notation $a + b$ denotes the
bitwise XOR of $a$ and $b$, i.e. the sum of $a$ and $b$ viewed
as elements of the additive group ${\mathbb{Z}}_2^n$. We call observables
$\{\cA(a)\}$ satisfying the first set of relations in~\eqref{eq:qblr-1} \emph{exactly linear}.

\begin{proof}
For every $u\in\{0,1\}^n$ consider the Fourier transform  $\hat{A}^u =
\E_{a} (-1)^{a\cdot u} A(a)$. Define measurement operators
  $B^u = (\hat{A}^u)^2$.
By Parseval's identity, these operators form a POVM. Using Naimark's theorem there exists an ancilla space $\mH'$, $\proj{\rm anc}\in\Density(\mH')$, and a projective
measurement $\{C^u\}$ on $\mH\otimes \mH'$ that simulates $\{B^u\}$. Introduce 
observables
\[ \cA(a) = \sum_{u} (-1)^{u\cdot a} C^u. \]
From the orthogonality of the projectors $C^u$ it follows that $\cA(a)
\cA(b) = \cA(a+b)$. Write 
\begin{align*}
  \E_{a} \CON_{\rho'}(A(a), \cA(a))
  &= \frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{2}\E_{a}\Re\Tr_{\rho'}\big( A(a)\cA(a)\big)\\
	&= \frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{2}\E_{a}\Re\Big(\sum_u \Trho\big( (-1)^{u\cdot a} A(a)(\hat{A}^u)^2\big)\Big)\\
	&= \frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{2}\sum_u \Trho\big((\hat{A}^u)^3\big).
\end{align*}
To conclude, note that
  $\sum_u \Trho((\hat{A}^u)^3) =\E_{ab} \Trho(A(a) A(b) A(a + b))$, and use the assumption made in the theorem and the relation between $\CON_{\rho'}$ and $\DIS_{\rho'}^2 $.
\end{proof}

Next we exhibit a two-player game such that any strategy which succeeds with
probability at least $1 - \eps$ in the game must satisfy the assumption~\eqref{eq:qblr-0} of
Theorem~\ref{thm:qblr} for some $\delta = O(\sqrt{\eps})$.

We make extensive use of a state-dependent distance
between measurements that has been frequently used in the context of
